regulators.name: European Union
regulators.regulatorName: European Data Protection Board (EDPB) & national supervisory authorities
regulators.summary: EU General Data Protection Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2016/679). Enforced by national supervisory authorities, coordinated by the European Data Protection Board.

requirements.title: 72-Hour Supervisory Authority Breach Notification
requirements.requirement: Upon detection of a personal data breach, the insurer must assess it and, where required, notify the supervisory authority within 72 hours of becoming aware. The pass condition is a documented, timestamped notification to the regulator delivered within the 72-hour window for all qualifying breach events.

requirements.title: Absolute direct-marketing opt-out enforcement
requirements.requirement: The organization must implement an absolute, unconditional opt-out mechanism for direct marketing such that, once a data subject exercises this right, all marketing communications and profiling for direct-marketing purposes are halted across every channel and downstream campaign job. The pass condition is that no direct-marketing material is sent and no marketing profile is built or used for that individual after opt-out is recorded.

requirements.title: Art. 9(2) Legal Basis Documentation for Special-Category Data
requirements.requirement: For every processing activity involving health, biometric, genetic, or other special-category data (including medical evidence in claims and underwriting), the organization must identify, document, and maintain a specific Art. 9(2) legal basis in its Records of Processing Activities (RoPA) before processing commences. Pass condition: no special-category data processing activity exists without a recorded, approved Art. 9(2) condition.

requirements.title: Audit Logging of Special-Category Data Access and Processing
requirements.requirement: All access to, and processing of, special-category data (reads, writes, exports, and deletions) must be captured in tamper-evident audit logs retained for the period required by applicable law. Pass condition: automated log coverage is verified across all special-category data systems, with no gaps, and logs are available for review upon regulatory inquiry or internal audit.

requirements.title: Audit Rights Provision in Processor Contracts
requirements.requirement: All DPAs must include contractual audit-rights clauses entitling the insurer to conduct or commission audits of each processor's and sub-processor's data protection controls. Pass condition: every executed DPA contains enforceable audit-rights language and evidence of at least one rights-exercise or assessment per contract term.

requirements.title: Automated Audit-Ready Evidence Capture
requirements.requirement: Controls must be instrumented to capture audit evidence automatically wherever technically feasible, including system-generated logs, access records, and compliance telemetry. Pass condition: an audit of any privacy control yields automatically produced, tamper-evident evidence without reliance solely on manual attestation.

requirements.title: Automated deletion or anonymisation at end of retention
requirements.requirement: Automated technical controls must execute deletion or irreversible anonymisation of identifiable data records upon expiry of their assigned retention period, without manual intervention being required to trigger the process. Pass condition: automated jobs demonstrably fire at or before the retention end-date for every data category, with no identifiable records surviving beyond their scheduled expiry.

requirements.title: Consent withdrawal mechanism — equally easy as granting
requirements.requirement: The insurer must provide data subjects with a mechanism to withdraw consent at any time that is no more burdensome than the method used to grant consent (e.g., if consent was granted via a single click on a web form, withdrawal must also be achievable via a single click). Pass condition: withdrawal pathway is present in every channel where consent is collected, completes in the same or fewer steps as granting, and triggers immediate cessation of processing for the withdrawn purpose.

requirements.title: Contestation Right & Remediation Process for Automated Decisions
requirements.requirement: The insurer must provide data subjects with a clearly communicated, accessible mechanism to contest the outcome of an automated decision and must document the investigation and resolution of each contest, including any remediation applied. Pass condition: all contests are logged, responded to within the prescribed timeframe, and outcomes are tracked for quality review.

requirements.title: DPO Formal Designation & Independence Requirement
requirements.requirement: The organization must formally designate a Data Protection Officer who is adequately resourced and structurally independent (i.e., not subject to instructions regarding the exercise of DPO tasks, with no conflicts of interest). Pass condition: a documented appointment record exists, the DPO's position is free from conflicting duties, and sufficient budget/staff support is allocated.

requirements.title: DPO Involvement in All Personal-Data Matters
requirements.requirement: The designated DPO must be systematically consulted and involved in all processes, projects, and decisions that involve the processing of personal data. Pass condition: documented evidence (e.g., project sign-off records, privacy impact assessment reviews) shows DPO participation across all relevant personal-data activities.

requirements.title: DPO as Data Subject Contact Point
requirements.requirement: The DPO must serve as the accessible contact point for data subjects exercising their rights (e.g., access, erasure, rectification) and addressing privacy inquiries. Pass condition: a published, functional mechanism routes data subject requests to the DPO and responses are managed within required timeframes.

requirements.title: DPO as Supervisory Authority Contact Point
requirements.requirement: The DPO must serve as the designated, publicly accessible contact point for the relevant data-protection supervisory authority on all matters relating to personal-data processing and compliance. Pass condition: regulator communications are routed to and handled by the DPO, and contact details are published/disclosed as required.

requirements.title: DSAR confirmation-of-processing response
requirements.requirement: Upon receipt of a Data Subject Access Request (DSAR), the insurer must confirm in writing whether or not the data subject's personal data is being processed, including the purposes, categories, and legal basis of that processing. The obligation is satisfied when every DSAR receives a documented confirmation-of-processing statement delivered to the data subject within one calendar month of the verified request.

requirements.title: DSAR data copy and processing metadata delivery
requirements.requirement: Upon a verified DSAR, the insurer must produce and transmit to the data subject a complete copy of all personal data held, together with associated processing metadata (retention periods, third-party recipients, data sources, and any automated decision-making logic). The obligation is satisfied when the complete data package plus metadata is delivered to the requestor within one calendar month of the verified request.

requirements.title: Data Collection Minimisation Enforcement
requirements.requirement: The organization must collect only personal data fields that are strictly necessary for the explicitly stated processing purpose. Pass condition: no data collection pipeline or intake form captures fields beyond those documented as necessary for the declared purpose.

requirements.title: Data Processing Agreement (DPA) Execution with Processors
requirements.requirement: Every processor and sub-processor engaged by the insurer must be bound by a written Art. 28-compliant Data Processing Agreement (DPA) before any personal data processing begins. Pass condition: 100% of active processors and sub-processors have a fully executed, current DPA on file that meets Art. 28 requirements.

requirements.title: Data Restore & Processing Resilience Capability
requirements.requirement: The insurer must establish and maintain a documented capability to restore availability and access to personal data in a timely manner following a physical or technical incident, including tested backup-and-restore procedures and resilience architecture for all personal data processing systems. Pass condition: restore capability is documented, assigned an RTO/RPO, and evidence of a successful restore test exists within the past review cycle.

requirements.title: Design-Time Rejection of Purposeless Fields
requirements.requirement: Data architecture, system design, and engineering processes must incorporate a control that automatically or procedurally rejects the inclusion of any data field that lacks a documented purpose prior to deployment. Pass condition: no field without a documented purpose can be promoted to production; evidenced by design review sign-off and pipeline validation rules.

requirements.title: Direct controller-to-controller data transmission mechanism
requirements.requirement: Where technically feasible, the insurer must establish and operate a capability to transmit a data subject's provided personal data directly to another designated controller upon the subject's instruction. The obligation is met when a verified portability request citing a receiving controller results in a successful, secure, direct transmission to that controller without requiring the subject to act as an intermediary.

requirements.title: Documented Privacy Policy Suite
requirements.requirement: The organization must maintain a complete, current set of documented privacy policies covering every privacy control obligation. Pass condition: an auditor can retrieve a version-controlled policy document for each applicable privacy control, with approval records and effective dates.

requirements.title: EU AI Act High-Risk Obligation Crosswalk for Automated Decision Systems
requirements.requirement: The insurer must produce and maintain a documented crosswalk mapping each in-scope automated decision system (automated underwriting, pricing, claims triage) to the applicable EU AI Act high-risk AI obligations (conformity assessment, risk management, human oversight, data governance, transparency, and logging requirements). Pass condition: the crosswalk is completed, reviewed by legal and AI governance, and updated whenever a system is materially changed or a new high-risk system is introduced.

requirements.title: Erasure from backups, caches, and logs
requirements.requirement: Upon verified erasure trigger, personal data must be purged or rendered irrecoverable from all backup systems, caches, and log repositories within a defined and documented retention schedule. Pass condition: backup/cache/log purge process is executed and evidenced for each valid erasure request, with no recoverable personal data remaining beyond the next scheduled purge cycle.

requirements.title: Erasure propagation to third-party processors
requirements.requirement: When a valid erasure request is fulfilled, the insurer must notify and confirm deletion with all downstream third-party data processors who hold or process the relevant personal data on its behalf. Pass condition: written confirmation of deletion is obtained from each processor within the required regulatory timeframe for every erasure event.

requirements.title: Heightened Safeguards Implementation for Special-Category Data
requirements.requirement: Technical and organizational safeguards beyond baseline data-protection controls (e.g., encryption at rest and in transit, pseudonymization, data minimization, and segregation of special-category data stores) must be designed, implemented, and maintained for all systems processing health, biometric, genetic, or other special-category data. Pass condition: a documented safeguard assessment confirms heightened controls are active for every special-category data store and processing pipeline.

requirements.title: High-Risk Breach Notification to Affected Data Subjects
requirements.requirement: Where a personal data breach is assessed as posing a high risk to the rights and freedoms of affected individuals, the insurer must notify those data subjects without undue delay. The pass condition is evidence of timely, individualized subject notifications for every high-risk breach, with no unjustified delay documented.

requirements.title: Human Review Mechanism for Automated Decisions
requirements.requirement: The insurer must establish and operationalize a process by which any individual subject to a solely automated decision with legal or similarly significant effects can request meaningful human review of that decision by a qualified employee with authority to override it. Pass condition: the human-review pathway is documented, tested, and completed within a defined SLA for each in-scope business line.

requirements.title: Instruction-Only Processing Obligation Enforcement
requirements.requirement: Processors must be contractually restricted to processing personal data solely on documented written instructions from the insurer, with any out-of-scope processing prohibited and tracked. Pass condition: DPAs include an instruction-only clause, and evidence of documented processing instructions exists for each active engagement with no record of unauthorised processing.

requirements.title: Lawful Basis Documentation per Processing Activity
requirements.requirement: Before any personal data is collected, each processing activity must have one documented Art. 6 lawful basis (consent, contract, legal obligation, vital interests, public task, or legitimate interests) recorded in the organization's processing activity inventory. Pass condition: every active processing activity in the inventory carries a pre-collection lawful basis entry with no gaps.

requirements.title: Lawful Ground Establishment for Automated Decisions
requirements.requirement: For each automated processing activity that produces decisions with legal or similarly significant effects (e.g., automated underwriting, pricing, claims triage), the insurer must identify, document, and establish a valid lawful basis before deployment. Pass condition: every in-scope automated decision system has a recorded, approved lawful ground that is reviewed at least annually and upon material change.

requirements.title: Legitimate-Interests Balancing Test Record
requirements.requirement: For every processing activity that relies on legitimate interests as its Art. 6 lawful basis, a documented balancing test must be completed and retained prior to data collection, demonstrating that the controller's interests are not overridden by the data subject's rights. Pass condition: no legitimate-interests basis is active without an accompanying, dated balancing test record stored in the processing activity inventory.

requirements.title: Machine-assisted DSAR fulfilment mechanism
requirements.requirement: The insurer must implement and maintain a machine-assisted (automated or tool-supported) workflow capable of locating, collating, and packaging a data subject's personal data and metadata across all in-scope systems to support timely DSAR responses. The obligation is satisfied when a documented, operational tooling solution demonstrably reduces manual effort and enables consistent completion of DSARs within the one-month statutory deadline.

requirements.title: Meaningful Logic Disclosure for Automated Decision Systems
requirements.requirement: For each automated decision system with legal or similarly significant effects, the insurer must produce and maintain consumer-facing disclosures that explain in plain language the logic, key inputs, and likely consequences of the automated processing. Pass condition: disclosures are accessible at or before the point of automated decision and are kept current with model changes.

requirements.title: Objection-to-processing flag enforcement at data layer
requirements.requirement: The organization must implement and maintain objection flags at the data layer such that, when a data subject objects to processing of their personal data under a legitimate-interest or public-task basis, the flag is applied immediately and respected by all downstream systems and jobs. The pass condition is that processing ceases for the objected purpose within the required response window and no downstream job overrides or ignores the flag.

requirements.title: Opt-in consent capture at point of collection
requirements.requirement: Where consent is the legal basis for processing personal data, the insurer must capture a freely-given, specific, informed, and unambiguous affirmative opt-in from the data subject before any processing occurs. Pass condition: no personal data is processed under a consent basis unless a documented, affirmative opt-in action (not pre-ticked box or silence) has been recorded for that specific purpose.

requirements.title: Per-Field Purpose Documentation Register
requirements.requirement: Every data field collected or stored must have a documented, approved business purpose recorded in a central data catalogue or register. Pass condition: 100% of active data fields map to at least one explicit, approved purpose statement with no undocumented fields present.

requirements.title: Per-data-category retention schedule documentation
requirements.requirement: The organization must maintain a documented, approved retention schedule that assigns a defined maximum retention period to each category of personal/identifiable data it holds. Pass condition: a current, comprehensive schedule exists covering all data categories, is reviewed at least annually, and is approved by the accountable owner.

requirements.title: Personal Data Accuracy Maintenance Mechanism
requirements.requirement: The organization must implement and operate ongoing controls and processes (e.g., data validation rules, periodic data quality reviews) that proactively keep personal data accurate and up-to-date across all systems of record. Pass condition: documented accuracy controls exist and evidence of regular data quality monitoring is maintained.

requirements.title: Personal Data Breach Detection & Assessment Process
requirements.requirement: The insurer must maintain an operational process to detect potential personal data breaches, triage them, and assess severity and notifiability. The pass condition is a documented, tested breach-detection-and-assessment workflow with defined roles, severity criteria, and evidence of execution for each incident.

requirements.title: Personal Data Breach Register
requirements.requirement: The insurer must maintain a breach register that records all personal data breaches, including their facts, effects, and remedial actions taken, regardless of whether notification was required. The pass condition is a current, complete register that is available for supervisory inspection at any time and is updated following every identified breach.

requirements.title: Personal Data Rectification Request Fulfillment Within One Month
requirements.requirement: Upon receipt of a data subject rectification request, the organization must correct inaccurate personal data across all relevant systems and confirm completion to the requestor within one calendar month. Pass condition: 100% of rectification requests are fulfilled and confirmed within 30 days of receipt, with a complete audit trail per request.

requirements.title: Pre-build DPIA completion & sign-off for high-risk processing
requirements.requirement: A Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) must be fully completed and formally signed off by the accountable owner before any build or processing activity commences where the intended processing is deemed high-risk to data subjects. The pass condition is a documented, approved DPIA on record prior to the start of build, evidencing identified risks, mitigating controls, and residual risk determination.

requirements.title: Prior supervisory authority consultation where residual risk remains high
requirements.requirement: Where a completed DPIA concludes that residual risk remains high and cannot be sufficiently mitigated by internal controls, the organisation must conduct prior consultation with the relevant supervisory authority (per Art. 36 GDPR) before processing begins. The pass condition is documented evidence of the consultation submission to the supervisory authority and receipt of its response (or expiry of the consultation period) prior to commencement of the high-risk processing.

requirements.title: Privacy Accountability Audit Readiness Programme
requirements.requirement: The organization must operate a formal accountability programme that aggregates policies, decision records, and evidence artefacts into an audit-ready package and periodically verifies completeness. Pass condition: a regulator or internal auditor can request and receive a full evidence pack for any privacy control within a defined SLA, with no material gaps identified.

requirements.title: Privacy Decision Record Maintenance
requirements.requirement: For each material privacy decision (e.g., lawful-basis determinations, DPIA outcomes, consent scope changes), a structured decision record must be created and retained. Pass condition: every qualifying decision has a retrievable, dated record that identifies the decision-maker, rationale, and outcome.

requirements.title: Privacy Notice Delivery at or Before Data Collection
requirements.requirement: A plain-language, layered privacy notice meeting Art. 13/14 content requirements must be presented to every data subject at or before the point of personal data collection. Pass condition: no personal data is collected without the compliant notice having been surfaced to the data subject through the relevant channel.

requirements.title: Privacy-by-Default System Configuration
requirements.requirement: All systems must default to the most privacy-protective settings available at the point of deployment and release, ensuring that no more personal data is processed than is necessary for each specified purpose without affirmative action by the user or administrator. Pass condition: release acceptance criteria include a verified privacy-default configuration check, confirmed by the Data Protection Officer before go-live.

requirements.title: Privacy-by-Design Architecture Embedding
requirements.requirement: Privacy controls — including pseudonymisation, data minimisation, and access limits — must be embedded into system and solution architecture from the inception of any new or materially changed system. Pass condition: architecture review artifacts demonstrate that privacy controls are incorporated at design stage prior to build commencement, with documented sign-off from the Data Protection Officer.

requirements.title: Processing-restriction flag enforcement at data layer
requirements.requirement: The organization must implement and maintain processing-restriction flags at the data layer such that, when a data subject invokes their right to restriction of processing, the flag is applied immediately and durably in the authoritative data store. The pass condition is that no downstream system, batch job, or pipeline reads or acts on restricted records for prohibited purposes while the flag is active.

requirements.title: Prohibition on Incompatible Secondary Use of Data
requirements.requirement: Personal data collected for one stated purpose must not be re-used for any secondary purpose that is incompatible with the original collection purpose, unless a fresh legal basis and purpose statement is documented and approved. Pass condition: no downstream use case or analytics workload processes personal data outside its documented compatible purpose scope, verified through data lineage and privacy impact reviews.

requirements.title: Prohibition on indefinite storage of identifiable data
requirements.requirement: No personal or otherwise identifiable data may be retained without an assigned, finite retention period; any data store containing identifiable records must be governed by the approved retention schedule. Pass condition: data inventory confirms zero data stores classified as 'indefinite' or 'retain until further notice' for identifiable data, verified through periodic data governance audits.

requirements.title: Rectification/erasure notification to data recipients (Art. 19)
requirements.requirement: Where personal data has been disclosed to recipients (e.g., reinsurers, service providers, analytics partners), the insurer must communicate any rectification or erasure to each recipient and maintain a log of notifications. Pass condition: every rectification or erasure event generates a timestamped notification record sent to all identified recipients, with acknowledgements retained.

requirements.title: Regular Effectiveness Testing of Security-of-Processing Controls
requirements.requirement: The insurer must conduct regular, scheduled testing of the effectiveness of all technical and organisational measures applied to personal data processing (including encryption, pseudonymisation, confidentiality, integrity, availability, and resilience controls), with results documented and remediation actions tracked. Pass condition: a testing schedule exists, test results are recorded at the required cadence, and findings are closed within defined SLAs.

requirements.title: Restrictive Access Controls for Special-Category Data
requirements.requirement: Access to health, biometric, genetic, and other special-category data must be restricted to only those roles with a documented business need, enforced through role-based access controls (RBAC) with approval workflows. Pass condition: quarterly access reviews demonstrate that no user or system account holds access to special-category data without a current, approved justification.

requirements.title: Risk-Appropriate Technical & Organisational Measures Implementation
requirements.requirement: The insurer must implement and maintain a documented suite of risk-appropriate technical and organisational measures — including encryption, pseudonymisation, confidentiality controls, integrity controls, availability controls, and resilience mechanisms — applied across all personal data processing systems. Pass condition: a current, approved controls inventory exists mapping each measure to identified processing risks, aligned to the Encryption and Application Security standards.

requirements.title: RoPA inventory creation and maintenance
requirements.requirement: The organization must maintain a living Records of Processing Activities (RoPA) inventory that documents, for each processing activity, the purpose of processing, categories of personal data, recipients, cross-border transfers, and retention periods. The inventory is considered compliant when it is complete, accurate, and accessible at all times as a living document.

requirements.title: RoPA update upon system or process change
requirements.requirement: Whenever a new system is introduced, an existing system is materially changed, or a processing activity is added, modified, or retired, the RoPA must be updated to reflect the change before or at the point of go-live. The pass condition is that no active processing activity exists without a current, accurate RoPA entry.

requirements.title: Served Notice Version Record Against Data Subject
requirements.requirement: The exact version of the privacy notice served to each data subject must be recorded and linked to that individual's record at the time of collection, creating a durable audit trail. Pass condition: a retrievable log exists showing which notice version was presented to which data subject and when, with no gaps for any collection event.

requirements.title: Structured machine-readable data export capability
requirements.requirement: The insurer must produce and maintain a mechanism that exports a data subject's provided personal data in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format (e.g., JSON or CSV) upon request. The obligation is met when any verified data subject request results in a complete, well-formed export delivered in at least one machine-readable format within the required response window.

requirements.title: Sub-Processor Authorisation Chain Documentation
requirements.requirement: A documented authorisation chain must be maintained for every sub-processor, recording the insurer's prior written approval (general or specific) and each link from controller to processor to sub-processor. Pass condition: a complete, up-to-date register exists showing the authorisation lineage for every sub-processor in use.

requirements.title: Supplementary Measures Implementation
requirements.requirement: Where a TIA identifies that the transfer mechanism alone does not ensure an essentially equivalent level of protection, the insurer must identify, implement, and document supplementary technical and/or organisational measures (e.g., encryption, pseudonymisation, contractual restrictions) before the transfer commences or continues. Pass condition: documented supplementary measures are in place and operational for every transfer where the TIA found a residual protection gap.

requirements.title: Timestamped consent record with notice version
requirements.requirement: For every consent collected, the insurer must store a durable consent record that captures the data subject identity, the specific purpose consented to, the exact timestamp of consent, and the version of the privacy notice presented at the time of collection. Pass condition: audit of any consent event can produce a complete, retrievable record containing all four elements within a reasonable retrieval window.

requirements.title: Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) Execution
requirements.requirement: Prior to each EEA personal data transfer, or upon material change in destination-country law or processing context, the insurer must complete and document a Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) evaluating the legal landscape and practical risks of the destination country (post-Schrems II). Pass condition: a completed, signed TIA exists for every active EEA data transfer relationship and is refreshed when circumstances change.

requirements.title: Valid Transfer Mechanism Maintenance
requirements.requirement: For every flow of personal data out of the EEA, the insurer must have a valid, documented legal transfer mechanism in place—adequacy decision, Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs), or Binding Corporate Rules (BCRs)—before the transfer occurs. Pass condition: every identified EEA-to-third-country data flow is covered by a current, executed transfer mechanism with no gaps.

requirements.title: Verified deletion across all primary data stores
requirements.requirement: When erasure conditions are met (per applicable regulation), the insurer must verifiably delete the data subject's personal data from all primary operational data stores, databases, and repositories. Pass condition: documented proof of deletion from each primary store exists for every valid erasure request.
